decision: Scan set: Drive 'Mazda 3 (Gen4)' -> Scans/Full Car.stl (58.4M tris, 2.9 GB), Rear Wing, Wing Removed, Side Skirt Door Open (Artec exports) + Mazda 3 CAD/Hatch Upper Trim Panel.stl and Hatch OEM Aero Kit Spoiler.stl. Skipped: Floor Mats Only (interior mats, not body) and every .STEP (CAD, not scan data)
why: Brief: best full car + listed part/state scans, only our scan data

decision: Full car decimated out of core first (ive decimate: 4 mm -> 3.82M tris for full-car moves, 2 mm -> 12.9M for close-ups, cropped to front/left/rear 2 mm blocks of 3.8-6.5M tris)
why: Biggest STL in the batch; style guide: <=4 mm full car, <=2 mm close-ups; crops keep Blender under 15 GB

decision: Levelled with projects/huracan-evo/tools/level.py (RANSAC ground plane, 158k inliers, normal tilted 2.9 deg; long axis -> Y, nose -Y) and the same transform applied to every Artec part scan (level.json)
why: Raw frame was tilted and yawed (diagonal in top view); one rigid transform keeps all states registered. Levelled length 4,462 mm = Mazda spec 4,460 mm

decision: Removed the scissor jack under the right sill and floor scraps (tools/clean_car.py: drop tris below 250 mm outside the wheel bands and below 60 mm everywhere) + ive crop + --drop-islands 3000
why: Car was scanned raised ~15 cm on jacks (sills bottom out at 280-300 mm); jack showed in the low side checks. A small jack-pad remnant on the right sill stays (attached to the pinch weld)

decision: Canonical frame = ive prep of car4.stl -> /home/user/media/mazda-3-gen4/prep/car4.json; every crop, composite and part prepped --like car4.json
why: Lesson: never re-normalise a part/state separately

decision: Rear Wing, Wing Removed, Side Skirt Door Open used at identity (Artec frame)
why: tools/regcheck.py: 97/100/85 % of points within 15 mm of the car, median 4.2/1.05/1.09 mm; ICP would only slide the wing along its skin. Red/cyan/green-over-grey renders sit on the car (checks/reg/reg.jpg)

decision: Hatch Upper Trim Panel = the rear wing (roof spoiler) itself: it is in inches in its own frame; scaled x25.4 and FPFH+RANSAC+ICP registered to the Rear Wing scan, fitness 0.964, rmse 3.3 mm, same pose 6/6 tries; it covers 92.7 % of the wing scan
why: So it is a cleaned mesh of the same part; showing both would duplicate one part in the explode. The raw Artec Rear Wing scan is used (raw-scan look), trim pose kept in reg_trim_rw.json

decision: OEM Aero Kit Spoiler does NOT register to this car (fitness 0.30-0.45 vs car, wing and wing-removed hatch, pose changes per try); it is a different spoiler design (1123 mm wide vs the car's 1183 mm wing)
why: Rendered every candidate pose over the car: it intersects the roof/hatch. It is shown only as a floating part in the exploded stack and never seated on the car

decision: Wing-off base: car4 minus wing skin (tris within 9 mm of the wing scan) + Wing Removed scan where >1.5 mm from the kept car (tools/wingoff.py, +79.8k tris)
why: Hatch under the wing sits within a few mm of the wing underside, so ferrari composite.py's test against the uncut car added only 14 tris and left black holes; 1.5 mm fills the mount area with its real bolt holes (checks/reg/wo2_0.png)
Side Skirt Door Open only covers the sill/jamb below 0.86 m; there is no door part scan and no cabin, so opening the door would expose a hollow car. The wing coming off is the 'panel off' beat

decision: Shot plan: s1 front-left 3/4 low turntable -> s2 rear-left 3/4 orbit -> s3 headlamp/bumper Kodo close-up (70 mm, 2 mm) -> s4 flank glide (door reflections, 2 mm) -> s5 tail lamp close-up (2 mm) -> s6 rear wing lifts off the hatch onto its mounts (Wing Removed state) -> s7 rear-high to top-down -> s8 exploded stack (wing + aero-kit spoiler) orbiting behind, reassembles -> ILLUMAESTHETIC logo
why: Brief: Temerario order (turntables/orbits, extreme close-ups, panels open where state scans allow, top-down, exploded view, logo); lighter scan set, so lean on turntables and Kodo close-ups

decision: Shots rendered with the Ferrari session's projects/ferrari-296/tools/shot.py (keyed camera + hinged/flying parts, house silver look) from my tools/shots.py specs
why: Brief: reuse sibling tools; one renderer keeps the house look identical across the batch

decision: Car's left side (+X) for every side/3-4 view
why: Right rear quarter has scan ribbing (vertical stripes) visible in the low right-side checks; left flank is clean

decision: s3 frames the left headlamp + bumper surfacing from the side at 70 mm; grille kept out of frame
why: Grille mesh is a holey scan (dark gaps) in the 30% previews; lamp top edge has small real gaps, acceptable at this size

decision: s4 aims into the car from behind the left rear wheel so the flank runs diagonally through the frame
why: First two previews left a third/half of the 9:16 frame black

decision: Exploded stack: wing rises 0.5 m and pitches 12-14 deg (underside to camera), aero-kit spoiler drops from above to hover 1.05 m over the wing; on reassembly the wing seats (ease-in lock) and the aero spoiler lifts out of frame
why: Only the wing is registered to the car; the aero spoiler is shown as a separate scanned part and never placed on the car. Parts stack above the car (portrait-friendly, lesson: don't fly parts at the lens)

decision: Logo: IllumaestheticLogo_V2COMPLETE_1.png from www.illumaesthetic.com header (transparent PNG, 6135x1059) -> remotion/public/illumaesthetic_logo.png (gitignored)
why: Brief: logo missing locally, get it from the website; the V2 has a transparent background that sits on the render black (the Color-01 has a white box)

decision: Render: 75 % res, 12 spp, 15 fps (minterpolate to 30 in assemble), one Blender job at a time via tools/render_queue.sh; 30 % previews ran with the final job paused (SIGSTOP)
why: Brief + lessons: serialise heavy jobs; ~13 s/frame
